title: The 10 Best Pipe Wrenches
subtitle: Aluminum and cast iron pipe wrenches and sets for plumbing, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A pipe wrench grips round pipe and fittings with teeth that bite harder as you turn. We ranked 10 best-sellers from RIDGID, Klein Tools, DURATECH, HURRICANE and value brands on rating, review volume and features (an aluminum handle, 2-inch or larger capacity, a multi-wrench set and replaceable jaws).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: Performance Tool W1133-10B 10 in. Red Pipe Wrench
avoid.verdict: A cheap 10-inch pipe wrench whose listing describes a different model and names a different manufacturer.
reasons: The title is for the 10-inch W1133-10B, but the first bullet describes the 'W1133-12B', a different size.
The spec table lists the manufacturer as 'WIOGW', not Performance Tool, so it's unclear who makes what ships.
The bullets give no capacity, jaw material or heat treatment, only generic phrases. The DURATECH 8-inch costs about the same and lists its 1/8 to 1 inch capacity and replaceable jaws.

buyers_guide.a: Aluminum wrenches are about 40% lighter with the same jaws, which matters when you use them overhead or all day. Cast iron is cheaper and fine for occasional use.
A 10- to 14-inch wrench handles most household pipe. An 18-inch reaches 2-1/2-inch pipe and gives more leverage. 24-inch and up is for large pipe and stubborn joints.
Use one wrench to hold the fitting and the other to turn the pipe, so you don't twist or crack the rest of the line.
The teeth bite to grip, so they mark the surface. Wrap chrome or finished pipe with a rag, or use a strap wrench instead.
On RIDGID and DURATECH-style wrenches, the hook jaw, heel jaw and spring can be replaced when the teeth wear, so the wrench lasts for decades.
